newsitem.title: FRANCE: British pilots on trial for French skydiver death.
newsitem.headline: British pilots on trial for French skydiver death.

text.p: Two British glider pilots went on trial in the southern French town on Gap on Wednesday charged with manslaughter after a skydiver crashed on to their aircraft in mid-air and died, court sources said.

The two pilots parachuted to safety after the collision, in June 1995 near the Alpine airfield of Gap-Tallard, north of Marseille, a training ground for experienced parachutists in the glider fans' favourite region of France.
Investigators' reports said the experienced 17-year-old French skydiver hit the glider at an altitude of 1,500 metres (5,000 ft) after free-falling 2,000 metres (6,600 ft).
He was knocked unconscious and plummeted to the ground with his parachute still unopened.

Spokesmen for the French Gliding and Parachuting Federations said the airspace around Gap-Tallard was open to both gliders and parachutists and the trial would establish if the pilots were guilty of manslaughter through negligence.
Court sources said the trial was expected to last one day only but it was not clear when the court would announce its verdict. The names of the pilots were not immediately available.
